verification: Independent referee pass on 2026-11-12: Codex gpt-6.1-sol (high), run on a separate machine with its own programs and no access to the repository code, read the public source line by line (commit 1ad6ed7). Verdict GAP with no counterexample to the theorem: the cost-time construction, the sprinkling rate bound, the compact return process and the survival continuity were each marked correct; four local repairs were requested and are in public_commit 4bd8c7cd: (1) the sprinkling chain keeps the order of arrivals in its state, because acceptance is not a function of the set of arrived edges; (2) a new lemma proves E F_k(G_n)/n -> P(|Er(P)| >= k) for independent budgets and for deterministic arrays from the cost-time local limit alone (comparison of G_n with G_n(t) after removing the vertices of budget above B), so the upper bound no longer rests on the scope of the cited local-limit theorem; (3) the remark on fixed points of the generating equation now says that the limit is identified through its bound below one on the compact set (the constant one is always a fixed point); (4) rank invariance is stated for costs with a common continuous law. The referee's own checks: exhaustive one-edge sensitivity of F_k on all graphs with 5 vertices and of the preference graph on K_4 (at most three kept edges change, the paper uses five), graph simulations at n = 500 and 2000, Erlang-tree Monte Carlo (20,000 trees a law) and quadrature of the generating equation (rho = 0.88557 for D = 3, 0.32327 for P(1) = 0.6, P(5) = 0.4, 0 for D = 2), all consistent with the paper. The new sandwich inequality was tested by brute force on 6,000 random instances with 5 to 14 vertices, no violation. Not checked by the referee: the exact statements of the cited theorems (no browsing) and novelty beyond memory.
